Human appearance assets and attribution

Body: Soldier.glb (renamed dancer.glb) from the three.js examples, originally
an Adobe Mixamo character. Integrated into this dance application.
Source: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/dev/examples/models/gltf/Soldier.glb
Mixamo usage terms: https://helpx.adobe.com/creative-cloud/faq/mixamo-faq.html

Face: Infinite, 3D Head Scan by Lee Perry-Smith, based on work at
www.triplegangers.com, licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported.
Original source: http://www.ir-ltd.net/
Distribution source: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/tree/dev/examples/models/gltf/LeePerrySmith
License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/
Original notice is reproduced in HEAD-LICENSE.txt.
The face geometry has been cropped below the neck, scaled and attached to a
replacement body. Its color and tangent-space normal maps are retained.
The scan has closed eyes; it is not a facial-expression or lip-sync model.

Motion: SambaDance skeletal performance from Michelle.glb in the three.js
examples, originally an Adobe Mixamo character/animation. dance-motion.glb
contains only its skeleton and animation tracks; the rendered Michelle mesh
and textures have been removed. Motion is retargeted onto the replacement body.
Source: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/dev/examples/models/gltf/Michelle.glb

GLTFLoader.js and toTrianglesDrawMode are from three.js r160, by the three.js
authors, under the MIT license reproduced in ../vendor/three.LICENSE.txt.
Only ES module imports/exports were adapted to the application's THREE global.
The existing renderer is also three.js r160. All assets are served locally;
no runtime CDN, Hugging Face inference service or paid API is required.
